item.title: Byakkotai Memorial, Mount Iimori: The Tragedy of the Teenage Samurai — Guide
item.description: The Byakkotai Memorial on Mount Iimori honours one of the most poignant episodes of the Boshin War — a unit of roughly 20 teenage samurai cadets, aged 16 to 17, who retreated to this hillside during the 1868 siege of Aizu-Wakamatsu and, seeing smoke rising from the castle town below, mistakenly believed Tsurugajo Castle had fallen. Rather than surrender, most took their own lives; one survivor’s account preserved their story. Their graves and a memorial statue now stand at the summit, alongside a curious gifted Roman column and Italian fascist-era monument.

item.title: Tsurugajo Castle, Aizu-Wakamatsu: A Samurai Stronghold Reborn — Guide
item.description: Tsurugajo Castle in Aizu-Wakamatsu is one of Japan’s most storied fortresses — the site of a month-long 1868 siege during the Boshin War, when Aizu samurai (including the teenage Byakkotai) made their last stand against imperial forces. The current five-storey keep, rebuilt in 1965 with a distinctive red-tile roof unique among Japanese castles, houses a museum on Aizu’s samurai history, and the surrounding park bursts into roughly 1,000 cherry trees each April.
